sources.title: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division: Country Profile, Turkey, August 2008
sources.note: Directly read 28-page institutional profile. Used only for republican foundation, geography, NATO accession and broad twentieth-century phases, not outdated current statistics or its problematic early-history simplifications. Legacy loc.gov/rr/frd/cs/profiles/Turkey.pdf is the same work.

sources.title: Grand National Assembly of Türkiye: History
sources.note: Direct official text read: 29 October 1923 republic, 1924 constitution, amendments of 1934 and 1937, 1960 intervention, 1971 memorandum, 1980 coup, 1982 constitution and 2018 implementation of presidential system.

sources.title: CRS: Turkey (Türkiye), Major Issues and U.S. Relations
sources.note: Jim Zanotti and Clayton Thomas; HTML version updated 15 September 2025, directly read. Domestic Issues section for 2016, 2017/2018 constitutional transition, election concerns, Kurdish rights and political competition. No live officeholder or future-election outcome claim.

sources.title: Atatürk Research Center, Atatürk Encyclopedia: Harf Devrimi
sources.note: Original indexed institutional article and reproduced law text checked; direct app is JavaScript-only. Law adopted 1 November 1928, published 3 November, Latin-based Turkish letters; implementation in offices and schools. Older /bilgi/harf-devrimi/?pdf=3622 is a mirror of this work.

sources.title: Constitutional Court of Türkiye: Anayasa, Article 6
sources.note: Original indexed official Turkish text checked: MADDE 6- Egemenlik, kayıtsız şartsız Milletindir. This is the Court’s modern text of the 1982 Constitution as amended, not an image of its first printing.

sources.title: Constitutional Court: Basic Legal Texts, Constitution of the Republic of Turkey
sources.note: Original indexed official English text checked, Article 6: Sovereignty belongs to the Nation without any restriction or condition. Direct PDF returned 502; ww2.anayasa.gov.tr mirror also failed. Turkish and English versions treated as one work in final budget.

sources.title: UNESCO Courier: Turkish coffee, not just a drink but a culture
sources.note: Direct text read; 2023 article. Preparation, social visits and some contemporary salty-coffee engagement customs only. Historical origin legends and the inaccurate coffee-to-Europe story are not adopted.

sources.title: UNESCO Decision 11.COM 10.B.2: Flatbread making and sharing culture
sources.note: 2016 multinational inscription decision, original indexed text read. Family/neighbour work, several baking technologies, and bread given to newlyweds’ neighbours specifically in Turkey. Direct page challenged. Treat as same work as element 01181.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ebru, Turkish art of marbling
sources.note: 2014 inscription, original indexed institutional description read; direct page challenged. Floating pigments, transfer to paper, bookbinding and apprenticeship. Do not repeat the page’s chemically imprecise description of ox-gall as an acid.

sources.title: WHO: Turkey, family practice for quality in universal health coverage
sources.note: Directly read institutional overview of 2018 case study: 2003 Health Transformation Plan, family/community centres, insurance and remaining pressures. WHO-HIS-SDS-2018.35-eng.pdf is the underlying same work; its indexed text was also checked, while direct PDF failed.

sources.title: UNICEF Türkiye: Healing Lives Through WASH Activities after the Devastating Earthquakes
sources.note: 28 July 2023, directly read. Named settlement, water trucking/testing/repairs, toilets/showers and family/baby hygiene kits. No national universal-access claim.

sources.title: UNICEF: Running towards a rebuilt future
sources.note: Elif Petek Samatyalı, 8 May 2023, directly read. Nine-year-old Meryem in Osmaniye, multiplication, temporary housing, games, siblings and teacher ambitions. No inference that this represents every displaced child.

sources.title: UNICEF: Learning the ABCs of child development in an earthquake zone
sources.note: Elif Petek Samatyalı, 5 December 2023, directly read. Parent sessions in Hatay container/tent surroundings, bilingual delivery for citizens and Syrian refugees, named mother Meryem and son Özgür. Descriptive reporting, not individual medical advice.

sources.title: UNICEF: Education Sector Needs Overview, May 2024
sources.note: Direct landing-page summary and original indexed PDF text checked. Survey of 4,156 households from diverse backgrounds; missing food, drinking water and toilets as education barriers. Percentages deliberately omitted; not a national prevalence estimate.

sources.title: Nobel Prize: Aziz Sancar, Facts
sources.note: Original indexed official text checked. Savur birth, parents’ encouragement, Istanbul/US education; 1983 bacterial DNA repair research, 2015 award. Tracking URL removed. Research was international and done abroad, not attributed exclusively to Turkish laboratories.

sources.title: Göbekli Tepe Research Staff: Over twenty-five years of research at Göbekli Tepe
sources.note: German Archaeological Institute project account, 16 January 2023, directly read. 1963 survey, local farmers reporting finds, 1994 revisit, Şanlıurfa Museum/DAI excavation from 1995 and interdisciplinary team. Modern discovery is distinguished from ancient construction.

proposedOverrides.name: Turkey (Türkiye)
proposedOverrides.summary: The republic founded in 1923 appears here from 1930, with changing institutions and diverse everyday lives.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Genuine missing HB record, circa 1930 to open end; no aliases associated. Ottoman and earlier Anatolian civilizations remain distinct. Decoded mainland in 1930 and 1938 stops at 39.35 E; 1945 and later reaches 44.793 E. Early eastern omission and late foundation start are publicly disclosed, without interpreting the change as a conquest. Current reporting is dated; exclusive final phase endpoint 2026 covers the researched 2025 political assessment, not an end of state. See identities.json.
